notes.title: How the cuisine filters were policed
notes.body: Every food card names a specific dish — a cuisine label alone doesn’t qualify. State College’s canon is a college town’s own: the Berkey Creamery (Penn State’s own ice cream), the grilled sticky at Ye Olde College Diner, tavern wings, Happy Valley craft beer (Otto’s, Robin Hood, Elk Creek), and the diner/breakfast institutions, sourced to the Centre Daily Times, StateCollege.com and Onward State. A cuisine tag names the kitchen’s own tradition, never one dish it happens to serve.

notes.title: Web-searched and fact-checked
notes.body: Every place is traceable to a credible source — the Centre Daily Times, StateCollege.com, Onward State, the Happy Valley Adventure Bureau, Uncovering PA, Atlas Obscura and official sites — recorded in data/sources.json. Every coordinate is verified into data/geocodes.json and every place status-checked open. Yelp/TripAdvisor never count toward the two-source bar.

places.w: 1854 engineering marvel: a three-track loop that let locomotives climb the Alleghenies for the first time, still an active Norfolk Southern main line with a train passing roughly every half hour. Funicular (when running) or 194 steps up to the trackside viewing area; small museum and gift shop. Designated a National Historic Landmark in 1966.

pv.src: Wikipedia published coords (Horseshoe Curve, Pennsylvania) 40°29'51.5"N 78°29'03"W

places.w: Three floors in the Pennsylvania Railroad's 1882 Master Mechanics Building telling the story of the men and women of 'Railroad City,' plus the Harry Bennett Memorial Roundhouse with a working 105-ft turntable and rolling stock. Also the ticketing gateway for Horseshoe Curve.

pv.src: Wikipedia published coords (Railroaders Memorial Museum) 40°30'52.01"N 78°23'57.01"W

places.w: Historic lakeside park, home to Leap-the-Dips (1902) — the world's oldest operating wooden roller coaster and a National Historic Landmark. Note: all rides have stayed closed since 2024 (declining attendance and insurance costs); for 2026 the park runs mini-golf, batting cages, courts, yard games and live-music events with free grounds admission.

pv.src: Wikipedia published coords (Leap-The-Dips, Lakemont Park) 40°28'15"N 78°23'48"W

places.w: 1849 Greek Revival ironmaster's mansion built for Elias Baker, now the Blair County Historical Society museum. Original Baker family furnishings — hand-carved Belgian furniture, French mirrors — and a table linked to the 1862 Loyal War Governors' Conference. Tours Fri-Sun; NRHP-listed.

pv.src: Wikipedia published coords (Baker Mansion) 40°29'26"N 78°24'30"W

places.ad: 4352 E Pleasant Valley Blvd, Tipton, PA 16684
places.w: Family-owned Italian-themed amusement park founded 1946 by the DelGrosso family, whose regional pasta-sauce brand is still made on-site. 30+ rides, America's only Italian-themed waterpark, free admission and parking, homemade pasta, and the annual Italian Food & Heritage Festival.

pv.src: Wikipedia infobox published coords (DelGrosso's Park) 40°38'09"N 78°17'46"W

places.w: Reconstructed 1778 Revolutionary War 'lead mine fort' in Sinking Valley — billed as America's westernmost Rev War site — with a log stockade, restored 19th-century farmhouse and barn, hiking trails and costumed interpreters. County-run park; NRHP-listed.

pv.src: Wikipedia published coords (Fort Roberdeau) 40°34'57"N 78°16'26"W

places.w: 1906 playhouse built by impresario I.C. Mishler and rebuilt after an early fire — one of the first U.S. buildings devoted entirely to theatre. Restored 1,900-seat, three-level venue, now home to the Altoona Community Theatre and Altoona Symphony Orchestra. NRHP-listed.

pv.src: Wikipedia/Wikidata published coords (Mishler Theatre) 40°30'59"N 78°24'07"W

places.w: Home of the Double-A Altoona Curve, named for the nearby Horseshoe Curve. A 1999 ballpark modeled on a railroad roundhouse, with a roller coaster beyond the outfield wall and a mountain backdrop — regularly called one of the prettiest parks in minor-league baseball.

pv.src: Wikipedia published coords (Peoples Natural Gas Field) 40°28'25"N 78°23'41"W

places.w: The oldest surviving narrow-gauge railroad east of the Rockies and a National Historic Landmark, revived by the EBT Foundation in 2020. Steam excursions behind restored locomotive No. 16, the original 1900-era machine shops and roundhouse, with track being rebuilt south toward Three Springs and Saltillo.

pv.src: EBT Orbisonia station, 421 Meadow St; coord consistent across multiple sources (station 40.241444,-77.898986). Wikipedia NHL article coords not machine-extractable via WebSearch; Orbisonia borough GNIS 40.24306,-77.89306 corroborates vicinity.

places.w: Two crystal caves discovered by highway blasting in 1930 and seen on a single hour-long guided tour — the only two-cave tour in Pennsylvania. Gemstone panning, nature trails and seasonal events (haunted cave, holiday tours) just west of Huntingdon on Route 22.

pv.src: Google Maps place pin data string !3d40.5075899!4d-78.0713076 (google.com/maps/place/Lincoln+Caverns)

places.n: Trough Creek State Park (Balanced Rock & Rainbow Falls)
places.ad: 16362 Little Valley Rd, James Creek, PA 16657
places.w: 541-acre scenic gorge where Great Trough Creek cuts through Terrace Mountain into Raystown Lake. A short trail passes 15-20 ft Rainbow Falls to Balanced Rock, a boulder perched improbably on a ledge — the park's signature landmark.

pv.src: Wikipedia published coords (Trough Creek State Park) 40°18'43"N 78°07'47"W

places.w: 423-acre park on the western edge of the Seven Mountains around a six-acre lake, wrapped in the 80,000-acre Rothrock State Forest. A preserved iron-furnace historic district recalls the charcoal-iron company town that thrived here 1834-1904; swimming, camping and trailheads for backpacking and mountain biking.

pv.src: Wikipedia published coords (Greenwood Furnace State Park) 40°39'02"N 77°45'16"W

places.w: A 170-acre community park near Grampian in Clearfield County built around 300-million-year-old Homewood Sandstone: house-sized outcrops rising up to 50 ft, riddled with arches, crevices and crawl-through passageways. Pavilion, camping and an open-air stage on site.

pv.src: Wikipedia published coords (Bilger's Rocks) 40°59'36"N 78°35'35"W

places.w: Once Pennsylvania's second-largest commercial show cave, beneath a foothill of Tussey Mountain along Spruce Creek. Open to the public 1929-2016; permanently closed since 2016. Kept here as a flagged landmark — do not present as a live visit.

pv.src: Place-precise coord (40.645408,-78.088367) from place lookup; Wikipedia (Indian Caverns) corroborates Spruce Creek location. Not a raw !3d!4d string, hence med.
pv.ss: Permanently closed Nov 1, 2016; Altoona Mirror 2018 sale story, Yelp/TripAdvisor 'CLOSED', Mid-Atlantic Karst Conservancy 'One Last Visit' 2017; now used for bat conservation

places.ad: Old Main, Pollock Rd, University Park, PA 16802
places.w: The symbolic heart of Penn State, crowning the hill above the campus mall. The 1930 Georgian building sits on the site of the original 1859 College Building of the Farmers' High School and houses the Land-Grant Frescoes by Henry Varnum Poor. Grounds open daily; the lawn is the campus's ceremonial gathering place.

pv.src: Wikidata/Wikipedia infobox — Old Main (Pennsylvania State University), 40°47′47.4″N 77°51′46.4″W

places.ad: Nittany Lion Shrine, Curtin Rd near Rec Hall, University Park, PA 16802
places.w: One of the most photographed landmarks in Pennsylvania: a crouching mountain lion carved by sculptor Heinz Warneke from a 13-ton block of Indiana limestone, given by the Class of 1940. Reopened to visitors after a 2021-2022 site renovation; free, open-air, always accessible.

pv.src: Wikidata Q15262405 / Wikipedia — 40°47′49″N 77°52′10″W

places.n: Beaver Stadium & Penn State All-Sports Museum
places.ad: Beaver Stadium, 1 Beaver Stadium, University Park, PA 16802
places.w: The 106,000-seat home of Penn State football and its All-Sports Museum, whose Upper and Lower galleries trace over a century of Nittany Lion athletics. Museum open Tue-Sat 10-4, Sun 12-4 (reduced winter hours; home-game-week changes); staff take guests to the club level for a view inside the bowl. Note: the stadium itself is under a multi-year renovation (Project Surge) through 2027.

pv.src: Wikipedia infobox — Beaver Stadium, 40°48′44″N 77°51′22″W (All-Sports Museum is inside the stadium)

places.ad: Palmer Museum of Art, The Arboretum at Penn State, Bigler Rd, University Park, PA 16802
places.w: Penn State's art museum in a striking 73,000-sq-ft Allied Works building that opened June 1, 2024 at the edge of the Arboretum, nearly doubling exhibition space to 20 galleries with a store, cafe and sculpture path. Free admission; a genuine regional cultural destination.

pv.src: Wikipedia infobox — Palmer Museum of Art, 40°48′25″N 77°52′05″W (new Arboretum building, 650 Bigler Rd)

places.n: The Arboretum at Penn State (H.O. Smith Botanic Gardens)
places.ad: The Arboretum at Penn State, Bigler Rd & Park Ave, University Park, PA 16802
places.w: 370 acres of gardens, meadows and woodland walks a mile west of Beaver Stadium, centered on the 10-acre H.O. Smith Botanic Gardens with pollinator habitats, water features, an Overlook Pavilion and a children's garden. Free admission, open dawn to dusk daily.

pv.src: Wikipedia infobox — The Arboretum at Penn State, 40.805051, -77.864088

places.w: A free insect museum across from the Berkey Creamery, reopened in 2022 after renovation, with a live arthropod zoo and a research collection of hundreds of thousands of specimens. Open to the public 10-4 Monday-Friday; admission free.

pv.src: Wikipedia — Frost Entomological Museum, 40°48′13″N 77°51′43″W

places.ad: High St & Allegheny St, Bellefonte, PA 16823
places.w: A remarkably intact Victorian county-seat downtown along Spring Creek, listed on the National Register, built during a 19th-century iron-and-industry boom and once home to seven Pennsylvania governors. Grand houses, the 1889 railroad station and a walkable core of shops and eateries. Free, self-guided.

pv.src: Wikipedia/NRHP #77001136 — 40°54′48″N 77°46′43″W (district center)

places.w: Bellefonte's 3.5-acre riverside park along Spring Creek, fed by the Big Spring that pours out 11+ million gallons a day and gave the town its name ("la belle fonte"). Riverwalk, the restored 1889 passenger station, gardens and an Underground Railroad history marker. Free, open daily.

pv.src: two agreeing area aggregators (40.9095/40.9109, -77.7817); adjacent to Gamble Mill & Big Spring — NOT a whitelisted place-pin, needs re-verify

places.w: A National Register grist mill (1786/1894) on Spring Creek in Bellefonte's waterfront district, extensively restored and reopened in 2021 as a boutique hotel, restaurant and cocktail bar. A landmark on the Riverwalk; dine or stay to see the interior.

pv.src: Wikipedia/NRHP #75001627 — Gamble Mill, 40°54′50″N 77°47′01″W

places.w: The headquarters of the American Philatelic Society, the world's largest nonprofit stamp-collectors' organization, in the restored 1900 Pennsylvania Match Factory. Highlights include a fully reconstructed century-old general store and post office, a library and galleries. Open to visitors; check hours.

pv.src: Wikipedia (American Philatelic Society / Research Library) — Match Factory, 40°54′33″N 77°47′01″W

places.n: Boalsburg Historic District (Birthplace of Memorial Day)
places.w: A walkable stone-and-clapboard village that claims the first Memorial Day observance, traced to an 1864 cemetery gathering; the town center is full of shops, cafes and 18th-19th-century buildings and celebrates with a large Memorial Day weekend of events. Free, self-guided.

pv.src: Wikipedia/NRHP #77001139 — 40°46′34″N 77°47′38″W (district center)

places.w: Pennsylvania's museum of the citizen-soldier, set on the 28th Division Shrine grounds in Boalsburg. CLOSED to the public since Dec 8, 2024 for a $3.4M modernization (HVAC, geothermal, preservation systems); the reopening, once slated for Feb 2026, has slipped to 2027. The outdoor grounds and memorials remain worth a look; galleries are shut.

pv.src: Wikipedia — Pennsylvania Military Museum, 40°46′55″N 77°47′43″W (51 Boal Ave site)
pv.ss: pamilmuseum.org visit page + worklist — galleries closed for renovation (grounds/28th Div Shrine remain)

places.w: The estate of the Boal family since 1789, whose Columbus Chapel — brought from Spain in 1909 by a Columbus descendant who married into the family — holds the explorer's admiral's desk, two relics of the True Cross and centuries of European art. Guided 90-minute tours Wed-Sun at 2pm; other times by appointment.

pv.src: Wikipedia — Boal Mansion, 40°46′44″N 77°48′01″W

places.ad: 1001 E College Ave, State College, PA 16801
places.w: The restored ironmaster's mansion of Centre Furnace — the 18th-century iron works whose owners helped found Penn State — now the home of the Centre County Historical Society and listed on the National Register. Furnished to the Moses Thompson era (1842-1891). Guided tours on posted days; grounds and gardens open.

places.ad: Mount Nittany trailhead, 500 Mount Nittany Rd, Lemont, PA 16827
places.w: The mountain that gives Happy Valley its identity, with 8 miles of trails and seven overlooks above the valley. The short climb to the Mike Lynch Overlook (marker #3, ~0.6 mi up) gives the classic view over State College and campus; the full loop is ~4.8 mi. Limited trailhead parking in Lemont; free.

pv.src: Wikipedia published summit coords (Mount Nittany) 40°48'41"N 77°48'25"W. Represents mountain summit; Mike Lynch Overlook sits on the summit ridge just below (trailhead is in Lemont).

places.ad: 222 Penns Cave Rd, Centre Hall, PA 16828
places.w: America's only all-water cavern, toured entirely by boat, plus a wildlife park with a bus safari and off-road mountain tours. Cavern tours run Feb-Dec (daily 9-4 hourly in summer); the farm-nature-wildlife park runs Apr 1-Nov (closed for winter through Mar 31). Paid admission; the cave boat tour is not wheelchair accessible.

pv.src: Wikipedia published coords (Penn's Cave and Hotel) 40°52'58"N 77°36'36"W

places.w: A 3,394-acre park atop the Allegheny Plateau built around a 250-acre lake and one of the state's finest bogs (1,992-acre Natural Area) with orchids and carnivorous plants. The half-mile boardwalk Bog Trail is the signature walk; 20 miles of trails, swimming and boating. Free day use; open year-round.

pv.src: Wikipedia published coords (Black Moshannon State Park) 40°54'44"N 78°03'25"W

places.ad: Rothrock State Forest, Bear Meadows Rd, Boalsburg, PA 16827
places.w: A 96,000-acre forest of ridgelines, rhododendron valleys and mixed-oak woods wrapping the south side of the valley, prized for hiking, mountain biking and vistas (Bear Meadows Natural Area, the Mid State and Standing Stone trails). A multi-year purpose-built trail project is adding up to 47 miles; the first 7.5 opened in 2025. Free.

pv.src: Wikipedia published coords (Rothrock State Forest) 40°42'36"N 77°49'06"W (forest centroid)

places.w: A 62-acre nature center less than two miles from campus, pairing a historic farmstead with a 50-acre limestone-fed wetland crossed by a boardwalk. Run by Centre Region Parks & Recreation; grounds free and open daily, with programs and a visitor barn. Good for families and birders.

pv.src: Google Maps place pin data string !3d40.8134389!4d-77.8343736 (google.com/maps/place/Millbrook+Marsh+Nature+Center)

places.w: The valley's four-season recreation hill: 14 ski/snowboard trails in winter and a summer Fun Centre with go-karts, mini-golf, batting cages, a skate park and driving range, plus an outdoor amphitheater for concerts. Paid activities; hours are seasonal.

places.w: Downtown Altoona's counter-and-booths diner since 1933, run by three generations of the Batrus/George family. Its griddle hotcakes are a local institution; a longtime stop on any Altoona diner crawl.

places.w: Depression-era Altoona candy maker founded by brothers Bill and Bob Boyer, who invented the Mallo Cup in 1936 — the first cup candy in America, still made downtown along with Smoothie peanut-butter cups. Factory outlet store on-site with the collectible 'Mallo Cup points.'

places.w: Historic Hollidaysburg hotel dating to 1835 on the Pennsylvania Canal / Allegheny Portage route, rebuilt in 1886 by a Bavarian brewmaster with a cut-block barroom added in 1905. Now a restored tavern for American plates, craft beer and cocktails inside the NRHP-listed Hollidaysburg Historic District.
